svg.title: MarkeTech backend: from start-up to an answered request
svg.desc: Panel A: the backend image runs entrypoint.sh, which applies the migrations, collects the static files, creates the administrator account if needed, then becomes Daphne on port 8000; Django reads config.settings.dev or config.settings.prod, chosen by DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE. Panel B: config/asgi.py sends HTTP to Django and the WebSocket /ws/ to Channels. Panel C: an HTTP request goes through the middleware chain and config/urls.py, then, for POST /api/applications/, through JobApplicationViewSet, its permissions and throttles, ApplySerializer and the models to the database. Panel D: after the save, an e-mail and a live signal leave on commit. Panel E: the applications of the backend.
svg.text: Daphne calls config/asgi.py for each connection
middleware, URL table, view, permissions, serializer, model
what create() starts once the application is saved
one folder per domain, each app with its own tests.py
MarkeTech backend: from start-up to an answered request
How the backend container starts, which door a connection takes, how an HTTP request travels through Django,
and what leaves after a write. Follow the numbers 1 to 15. Real files of the repository, branch main.
THE IMAGE AND ITS START-UP SCRIPT: every time the backend container starts

svg.text: The e-mail and the signal leave only once the change is in the database: never for a write that was rolled back, never
before the page could read it. A failed send is written to the log and never breaks the user's action.
Here no transaction is open any more (no ATOMIC_REQUESTS), so on_commit runs at once: the e-mail leaves during the request.
